header: Date: 2026-08-12 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes | Attendees: Sophie Liu (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Anita Gomez (CSM), Priya Patel (Nimbus Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Nimbus Infra), Lena Morris (Product), Omar Farouk (Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access setup (VPC, IAM, KMS), review of this week's pilot results (latency and token cost), tuning suggestions (batching, prefix caching, quantization), and next steps for benchmark and security docs.
topics: Tuning and config suggestions (batching, cache, quantization)
transcript: 00:00 Sophie: hey everyone good morning, thanks for joining. we got about 45 minutes on the agenda — quick status, results review, and next steps.
00:12 Priya: morning, thanks. quick note, we have Daniel and Omar from infra/sec here as well.
00:18 Marco: great — i'll kick off with the results we ran this week. small disclaimer, the runs were on the hosted variant while we finish the vpc creds so numbers aren't final.
00:30 Marco: 1k synthetic queries, mix of short and mid-context prompts, median latency ~220ms on the r-infer-large model, p95 ~480ms, token cost approx $0.003 per request after prefix caching.
00:45 Priya: that p95 seems a bit high compared to our SLO of 300ms. is that because of cold starts or batching?
00:52 Marco: mostly a few cold starts — also we saw variance when batching was disabled for some streams. enabling continuous batching with target batch size 8 dropped p95 to ~320ms in our trial.
01:05 Daniel: just to clarify, when you say hosted variant, is that the shared tenancy or dedicated?
01:10 Marco: hosted shared right now — dedicated would give more predictable tail latency. for the POC we can test a small dedicated pool.
01:18 Sophie: quick commercial note — dedicated sizing estimate was shared in the PRD, but we can do a short dedicated pilot for 2 weeks if Nimbus wants to validate tail latencies.
01:28 Lena: cost question — going dedicated would bump price; do you have ballparks?
01:34 Sophie: ballpark depends on throughput. for your ~200 qps equivalent burst we estimated $Xk/month — i'll follow up with exact numbers.
01:42 Priya: back to tuning — you mentioned prefix/KV cache; do you have guidance for our prompt templates? we have a lot of repeated system instructions.

01:50 Marco: yes, if your prompts have a stable system prefix we can enable prefix caching; that cut tokenize time and saves repeated compute. also recommend keeping prompt history trimmed to last 3 messages for chat-like flows.
02:03 Priya: perfect, we'll prepare a set of canonical prompt templates.
02:08 Omar: security items — we need to confirm KMS integration and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys in the private deployment.

02:15 Sophie: yes we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated via KMS or HSM options; we'll share the KMS integration guide. for hosted we encrypt at rest with our keys but can offer BYOK for enterprise contracts.
02:28 Omar: also need details on audit logs and retention, and SAML SSO setup.
02:33 Anita: action — i'll attach the security packet and an SSO setup doc after the call.
02:38 Daniel: about access — we're blocked on providing the VPC peering details. daniel to provide the subnet cidrs and service account list by Monday.
02:48 Sophie: noted — once we have that Marco can spin up a temporary private test cluster in our staging to run the end-to-end onboarding.

02:56 Marco: small technical note from the runs: quantized int8 model lowered memory usage ~40% and increased throughput, but we saw a small drop in quality on one of your long-form prompts. we can run a targeted eval vs your prompts.
03:12 Priya: quality tradeoff is a concern; we need to keep NLU accuracy above 92% on our entity extraction tasks. can you run the same eval?
03:20 Marco: yes — please send the eval set and we'll run both fp16 and int8 variants and share confusion matrices.
03:28 Priya: will do.
03:31 Lena: curious about observability — do you expose per-route latency, token counts, and per-call trace ids?
03:39 Marco: yes — Redwood Console shows per-model and per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and trace ids you can correlate with your logs. we'll send dashboard screenshots.

03:48 Sophie: comps — you asked about other vendors; we heard BigCloudAI and VertexAI mentioned last week. Redwood differentiator is the hosting + private parity and the caching/batching knobs for cost control.
04:00 Priya: timeline check — our internal deadline to decide is end of September.
04:05 Sophie: that gives us time for two more benchmark cycles and a security review by mid-September.
04:10 Marco: proposed next technical milestone: run the dedicated 2-node pilot in staging (if you approve), run 10k mixed queries, and provide p50/p95/p99 and token cost breakdowns.
04:22 Daniel: confirm we want the dedicated pilot; Daniel to provision the VPC endpoints and credentials once we sync offline.
04:28 Omar: also want to know data residency — our legal team requires EU data to stay in eu-west-1 for GDPR scope. can Redwood pin region?
04:36 Sophie: yes we can pin region for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API can be routed to eu region but we'll confirm residency guarantees in the security packet.
04:45 Priya: last question — can you support service accounts and role-based access so we can limit who can deploy models?
04:51 Marco: yes RBAC is supported; we'll include the roles doc.

04:55 Sophie: recap and owners — Sophie to send SOC2 packet and pricing follow-up; Marco to run quantized vs fp16 evals and dedicated pilot bench; Daniel to provide VPC/subnet/CIDR and service account list; Omar to confirm KMS/HSM requirement; Priya to send eval set and canonical prompts.
05:12 Priya: thanks everyone, that sounds good.
05:15 Sophie: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and a proposed time for the sizing call. bye.
05:20 (call ends)
